sources.title: Joint Strategic Needs Assessments
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's JSNA provides evidence on population health needs, including ward-level data where available, to inform planning and arrangement of health, wellbeing and social-care services; it is needs evidence rather than parcel-specific capacity.

sources.title: Healthy streets
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's Healthy Streets JSNA brings together indicators including active travel, air quality, noise, accessibility and perceived safety; borough and street-health evidence is contextual until spatially matched to a parcel.

sources.title: Our Public Health work
sources.verified_claim: Havering states its Health in All Policies approach requires major policy decisions across housing, planning, transport, employment and the environment to consider health and health inequalities; this is governance context, not a parcel outcome.

sources.title: Our population
sources.verified_claim: Havering uses population and health intelligence for service planning and highlights an ageing population, a rapidly growing 0-4 population and local health inequalities; these are borough-level capacity signals rather than site-specific infrastructure proof.

sources.title: JSNA Review Survey
sources.verified_claim: Havering's JSNA review records stakeholder feedback and states a three-year delivery plan was scheduled from April 2026 to improve health-intelligence products; review status does not establish development capacity at a sample parcel.

sources.title: Joint Strategic Needs Assessment - JSNA
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's JSNA is the statutory process for identifying current and future health, wellbeing and social-care needs, including wider determinants such as housing, employment and income; it is population evidence, not parcel proof.

sources.title: Health and Wellbeing Strategy 2023-2028
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth's Health and Wellbeing Strategy prioritises health inequalities and wider determinants including housing, the economy, employment and the environment; strategic direction is not a site-specific development or health-capacity decision.

sources.title: Chapter 5 Social Infrastructure
sources.verified_claim: London Plan Policies S1-S2 require needs assessment for social infrastructure and collaboration with health bodies to identify future health and social-care provision, especially in growth or under-provided areas; policy does not establish a sample parcel's capacity.
